title: A Landfall for the Provision
premise: Yara Eriksen, a salvage diver scraping a living off the wreck of the Provision—a naval vessel that sank in forbidden waters decades ago—joins a ragtag expedition upriver when her salvaged artifacts begin drawing dangerous attention. When the expedition's radio goes silent and its members vanish one by one, Yara realizes the navy's silence about the Provision hides a living secret: survivors' descendants who never left, guarding a settlement that was never meant to exist. Following the river to its source, Yara must choose between selling out the hidden community that claims her as one of their own and protecting the found family she never expected. In the end, she floods the evidence rather than surrender it, sinking the Provision's last secrets—and herself into a new home.
about_author: O. M. Crane is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent six years charting remote northern waterways before turning to fiction. Their novels blend hard-edged adventure with quiet meditations on what it means to belong somewhere no map acknowledges.

chapters.title: Cold Work
chapters.summary: Yara dives the Provision's flooded hull alone at dawn, hauling up a sealed strongbox while dodging a navy patrol boat. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking a hunger for something more than salvage money.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: A smooth-talking antiquities dealer offers Yara triple value for the strongbox contents—old naval documents—then asks questions about coordinates she never gave him. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: unease; the wreck is watching back.

chapters.title: Expedition Upriver
chapters.summary: The dealer funds an expedition to trace the Provision's final voyage upstream, hiring Yara as diver and guide alongside botanist Teo, ex-soldier Marsh, and radio operator Ines. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: reluctant camaraderie forming among strangers.

chapters.title: Signs of Passage
chapters.summary: Days upriver, the crew finds fresh-cut wood and a child's moccasin miles from any registered settlement. Marsh insists it's nothing; Ines logs it anyway. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: creeping doubt beneath expedition bravado.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: A storm knocks out the radio mid-transmission to the dealer's base camp. That night someone takes two days of rations and the backup antenna. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: paranoia fraying trust; Marsh suspects his own crew.

chapters.title: Teo's Silence
chapters.summary: Teo vanishes during a portage, leaving only his notebook filled with sketches of terraced gardens that shouldn't exist. Yara dives a deep pool for his body and finds none. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Watchers
chapters.summary: Marsh spots figures on the ridge at dusk; shots are fired—not at them, but over them, a warning. Ines repairs the radio enough to send one garbled distress call. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: fear curdling into aggression he can't control.

chapters.title: Ines Gone
chapters.summary: They wake to find Ines taken and her radio dismantled with expert care—taken, not stolen. Yara reads the scene differently than Marsh: this was rescue, not abduction. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: first flicker of sympathy for the unseen river people.

chapters.title: Split Currents
chapters.summary: Marsh wants to track the abductors with force; Yara argues they'll all die trying. They split supplies, and Marsh marches off alone with the rifle. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: pride and grief driving a man past reason.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Old Chart
chapters.summary: Running rapids marked on a century-old chart, Yara capsizes and is pulled under—then hauled out by hands that know the water. She wakes in a warm room smelling of woodsmoke. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror dissolving into bewildered safety.

chapters.title: Haven at the Source
chapters.summary: Yara meets the river community: descendants of the Provision's crew who jumped ship rather than return from a mission ordered to erase itself. Elder Sanna recognizes Eriksen—her grandmother's name. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: shock of inheritance; a door opening onto family.

chapters.title: What the Navy Forgot
chapters.summary: Sanna tells the truth: the Provision carried orders to scuttle evidence of a massacre, and the crew refused, faking the wreck and building lives here. The dealer works for descendants of the officers who want proof destroyed—or leverage gained. POV: Sanna. Emotional beat: history as wound and bond.

chapters.title: Ines Among Them
chapters.summary: Yara finds Ines healthy, teaching children morse code by choice; Teo is cataloguing plants no outsider has named. Both warn her: once you've seen Haven, leaving is complicated. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging weighed against loyalty to the world left behind.

chapters.title: Marsh Arrives
chapters.summary: Half-dead, Marsh stumbles into Haven and sees only captors and collaborators. He demands Yara help him signal the dealer's base camp downstream. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: a good man broken by loss, unable to accept kindness from strangers.

chapters.title: The Strongbox Decision
chapters.summary: Yara reveals she still holds the strongbox key and knows where the Provision's true logbook lies in the drowned hull. Sanna asks her to sink it forever; the community votes, and Yara has the deciding voice. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the weight of being trusted by people who owe her nothing.

chapters.title: Marsh's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marsh slips away at night, stealing a skiff and the repaired radio. By dawn he's transmitted Haven's approximate location to the dealer's base camp. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: betrayal born not of malice but of a need for the mission to mean something.

chapters.title: Downriver Race
chapters.summary: Yara, Ines, and Haven's best boatmen race the current to intercept the dealer's team before they reach the wreck site. Rapids, a storm, and a near-drowning test every bond. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: fighting for a home she's known less than a week.

chapters.title: The Dealer's Terms
chapters.summary: They reach the base camp too late—the dealer's divers are already at the Provision. He offers Yara wealth and immunity if she guides them to the logbook, revealing he knows her grandmother was aboard. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: temptation weaponized through bloodline.

chapters.title: Flooded Hold
chapters.summary: In the Provision's black hold, Yara leads the dealer's divers astray while Ines jams their surface line. A collapse traps the dealer below; Yara could save him or take the logbook and go. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the wilderness forgives nothing—but she isn't the wilderness.

chapters.title: What She Saved
chapters.summary: Yara drags the dealer out, then lets the river take the logbook into silt forever. Marsh, witnessing her mercy, breaks down and confesses his transmission; together they misdirect the incoming navy response. POV: Marsh. Emotional beat: redemption earned through costly honesty.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The navy finds nothing but a legend; the dealer, half-drowned and discredited, retreats. Yara surfaces at Haven's dock as the community gathers—not as a guest, but as kin carrying her grandmother's name home. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: arrival after a lifetime adrift.

chapters.title: The River Remembers
chapters.summary: Seasons later, Yara trains Haven's young divers in the old wreck's safe passages, and Ines's radio crackles with weather reports instead of distress calls. Some maps stay unmarked; some families are chosen by rivers. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace—the belonging she dove for all along.
